set.prevailing_wage_basis: Project-dependent. 2026 SHRA Multifamily Lending Policies (County), Section 6.1: state and federal law require prevailing wages on projects receiving governmental benefits; 6.1.1 names the main state exemption, a below-market-rate loan on a project with at least 40% of units restricted at 80% AMI for at least 20 years (Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E)); 6.1.2 Davis-Bacon applies if the deal also has HOME at 12+ units or CDBG at 8+ units; 6.1.3 pay the higher rate when both apply. Loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b); the outcome depends on loan terms and the restricted-unit share of the project, so left unclear. Sources: https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-County-final.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

reason: No rule sets a fixed answer; SHRA policy 6.1 and Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) make it depend on loan terms and restricted-unit share.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: False for the bond financing itself. DIR coverage determinations PW 2006-001 Horizons at Indio (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf) and PW 2006-020(A) Heber (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe, hold that conduit multifamily revenue bonds, where the issuer assigns its rights to a private trustee that advances proceeds to the borrower and receives repayments directly, are not payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4). SHRA's structure matches: 2026 SHRA County Multifamily Lending and Bond Policies Section 9.1.3 state there is no liability to or pledge of the County's, the Housing Authority's or SHRA's faith, credit or taxing power, repayment is limited to private project revenues, and the program is self-supporting with the developer paying all costs; Section 9.4.11 provides a bank bond trustee as custodian of funds. Caveat: SHRA gap loans, HOME, CDBG or other public funds in the same deal are tested separately under SHRA policy 6.1 and Labor Code 1720 (1720(c)(5)(E) exemption; Davis-Bacon for HOME at 12+ or CDBG at 8+ units). Sources: https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-County-final.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Set false on DIR determinations PW 2006-001 and PW 2006-020(A) for trustee-structured conduit bonds, which matches SHRA policy 9.1.3 and 9.4.11; other public funds in the deal still need their own prevailing wage test.

reason: DIR determinations PW 2006-001 and 2006-020(A) hold trustee-structured conduit bonds are not public funds, and SHRA policy 9.1.3 and 9.4.11 match that structure.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Unresolved. The County fee deferral page (Chapter 16.100) states no prevailing wage rule. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, but 1720(c) exemptions (including de minimis and the 1720(c)(5) residential exemptions) and the other funding in the deal decide coverage. Sources: https://feedeferral.saccounty.gov/us/en/affordable-housing.html ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Left unclear: only basis is Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (waived fees are public funds); outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

reason: County page states no rule and Labor Code 1720(b)(4) alone does not settle coverage, which depends on 1720(c) exemptions.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Unresolved. The August 26, 2025 staff report on the AHL Program Guidelines (Resolution 11427) and the housing funds staff report state no prevailing wage rule for City loans (the latter notes only that Homekey and Infill Infrastructure require it). City loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b); the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption for below-market loans with 40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years may apply depending on loan terms. Davis-Bacon applies only if City HOME (12+ units) or CDBG (8+ units) is layered. Sources: https://mccmeetingspublic.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/folsomca-meet-20667254009747e4aa5f68a4d63539d6/ITEM-Attachment-001-3c80e00338b5420aafa72ac45dae4a5d.pdf ; https://mccmeetingspublic.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/folsomca-meet-20667254009747e4aa5f68a4d63539d6/ITEM-Attachment-001-54dff11a603148f68a0203d4b6b13245.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

reason: Folsom staff reports state no rule, so coverage rests on Labor Code 1720(b) and the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption, which depend on project facts.
